walkthroughs.body_html: At an equinox the Sun lies on the celestial equator (Dec ~ 0). At the summer solstice the Sun reaches its highest declination (+23.5 degrees), giving the longest daylight in the northern hemisphere.

The Earth rotates once relative to the stars in ~23 h 56 min (sidereal day). Because Earth has also moved along its orbit, it takes ~4 extra minutes for the Sun to return to the same meridian — giving a 24 h solar day.
For 'explain why a star rises 4 minutes earlier each night': link sidereal vs solar day, Earth's orbital motion (~1 deg/day), and how this offsets star return times.
